about: The queue plugin's texts and hooks, run by plugins/queue/tests/queue.rs. describe: the queue tool's text from a cqd status reply (cqd) or a /proc snapshot (snap). history: queue_history's text from cqd's rows, in UTC. wrap and env: how sessions run under claude-queue ({lib} and {run} are the test's folders). triggers: whether a queue_wait target is valid.

describe.name: cqd: grants closed, a bench, holders running, detached and external, two waiters, frozen, a hog
describe.want:
GRANTS CLOSED: cqd saw a GPU/NPU fault in the kernel log. Check dmesg; the user reopens them with `cq grants on`.
A bench is running: queued GPU/NPU opens wait for it.
GPU/NPU turn held by:
- L3 pid 4242 (shikigami npu-dma) python bench.py --long: holds gpu+npu for 10 min (running), ~5 min left, memory 6.5 GB (needs ~8), GPU busy 87%
- L4 pid 0 (gone) ./old: holds gpu for 15 min (detached), past its usual duration, memory 1 GB (needs ~1) [STUCK: its command ended but it still holds the turn]
- L5 pid 99 (seimei (you)) make: holds gpu for 10s (running), duration unknown, memory 0.5 GB (needs ~2.0)
- pid 777 blender: outside the queue, holds /dev/dri/renderD128 for 1 min, idle 30s
Waiting:
- #1 pid 5151 (seimei (you)) llama-bench -m x: waited 11 min, starts in ~2 min, blocked by L3 (npu_dma)
- #2 pid 5152 (other) ollama run: waited 30s, blocked by a running bench
Frozen by a bench: w_a, w_b.
12.5 GiB memory free, headroom 4.0 GB. 3 desktop processes outside the queue (desktop, browsers, open_app) use the GPU too; they never block the queue.
Idle memory hog: llama holds 20.1 GB, idle 45 min.
A stuck holder is usually an app restarted from an agent's shell. It keeps the turn until it quits; ask the user before closing a window they use. Restart it outside the queue with open_app or `env -u LD_PRELOAD systemd-run --user --collect <app>`.

describe.name: cqd: an empty queue
describe.want:
No queued command holds the GPU/NPU turn.
Nothing waits.
30.0 GiB memory free, headroom 10 GB. 0 desktop processes outside the queue (desktop, browsers, open_app) use the GPU too; they never block the queue.

- pid 11 (y) firefox: holds /dev/dri/renderD128 for 59s, RSS 0.0 GiB, GPU memory 0.0 GiB [graphics app, no compute device]

(cqd is not running: this view comes from /proc, without ETAs.)
